public_rationale: The contract tests whether Hegseth's own directives or speeches from around the February 26, 2026 post push AI deployment across the whole department at maximum speed, as a headline priority. Hegseth signed a memo on January 9, 2026, made available January 12, titled "Artificial Intelligence Strategy for the Department of War." It directs the department to become an "AI-first" warfighting force "across all components, from front to back" (e1). Its "Speed Wins" section says "the risks of not moving fast enough outweigh the risks of imperfect alignment" (e2). The memo falls within the target period of October 1, 2025 to February 26, 2026. It covers the whole department, puts speed first, and is a signed strategy addressed to senior leadership, so it meets the support condition. The packet contains nothing showing a cautious or low-priority approach, so the contradiction condition is not met. An AP report published February 24, 2026 says that in a January speech at SpaceX, Hegseth said he was shrugging off AI models "that won't allow you to fight wars" (e3). That remark is about which models to use, not how fast to adopt them, and the grade does not rest on it. The claim's mention of his career is about motive, which this evidence cannot test.
limitations: The evidence does not show Hegseth's motive or how he sees his career. It shows only his public directives and statements.
The memo was read from a third-party mirror because the official copy returned HTTP 403.
The January speech is known only through AP's short summary, with no exact date. It concerns rejecting restricted AI models, not the pace of adoption.
The packet does not show how AI ranks against Hegseth's other priorities, and it came from only two searches.
